title: Sens. Probe Meta For Claiming Tax Credits On AI Data Centers
key_facts: Democratic senators led by Ron Wyden wrote to Mark Zuckerberg on Tuesday (13 Oct 2026).
They say Meta is violating 'the spirit and, potentially, the letter' of federal tax law by using the research credit for its AI data center buildout.
Meta's filings say it cut its federal tax liability by $6.6 billion from 2023 to 2025 with the research credit.
The New York Times reported last month that Meta calls its data centers 'a giant experiment that could fail' and 'pilot models' in tax filings.
Meta warns in filings that the IRS may overturn the savings.
About a week earlier more than two dozen House Democrats wrote to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on 7 Oct.
quote_evidence: A group of Democratic senators wrote Tuesday that Meta is violating "the spirit and, potentially, the letter" of federal tax law by using a research and development tax credit to save billions of dollars on its massive data center buildout.
"While it remains unclear exactly how Meta was able to reduce its federal tax liability by over $6.6 billion in the last three years using federal research credits..."
why_it_matters_hint: Lawmakers question a large tax saving tied to data center building.
notes: Progressive outlet; no Meta response in the text.
